::: {#case .lx-sec}
```{=html}
<div class="lx-case">
<div class="lx-case-part"><p class="lx-eyebrow">1 · The puzzle</p><p>Grid electricity is cleaner in some hours than in others. If some electricity use moves into the cleaner hours, without using less in total, how much CO₂ does that save?</p><p class="lx-hint">Words first: <span class="lx-term" data-term="attributed-emissions">attributed emissions</span> are a share of the grid's CO₂ assigned to a user; <span class="lx-term" data-term="carbon-intensity">intensity</span> is CO₂ per MWh; a <span class="lx-term" data-term="optimization-window">window</span> is the stretch of time within which use may move.</p></div>
<div class="lx-case-part"><p class="lx-eyebrow">2 · The question in one sentence</p><p class="lx-case-q">How much do the <span class="lx-term" data-term="attributed-emissions">emissions attributed</span> to electricity consumption fall when load is re-timed according to hourly average grid <span class="lx-term" data-term="carbon-intensity">emission intensity</span> across U.S. regions, and which strategies suit which types of grid?</p><p class="lx-hint">Question type: descriptive (how much?), with a prescriptive part (which strategy suits which grid?).</p></div>
<div class="lx-case-part"><p class="lx-eyebrow">3 · Scale and boundary</p><ul><li><b>Inside:</b> U.S. grid regions, every hour of 2023, and each region's load, moved within <span class="lx-term" data-term="optimization-window">windows</span> of a month, a quarter or a year.</li><li><b>Left out:</b> which plants actually change output when load moves, forecast errors, and the cost of moving load beyond a penalty.</li></ul></div>
<div class="lx-case-part"><p class="lx-eyebrow">4 · Decisions, goal and rules, in words</p><ul><li><b>Decisions:</b> how much each hour's load moves up or down.</li><li><b>Goal:</b> the lowest attributed emissions over the window, plus a <span class="lx-term" data-term="penalty">penalty</span> for each adjusted hour.</li><li><b>Rules:</b> the window's total use does not fall; no hour moves beyond the allowed range, such as ±5%.</li></ul></div>
<div class="lx-case-part wide"><p class="lx-eyebrow">5 · Data and method</p><ul><li>A <span class="lx-term" data-term="mixed-integer-program">mixed-integer</span> load-regulation model, solved for each window with EIA's hourly data for 2023.</li><li>Regions are grouped by renewable share, the diversity of their generation and how much their intensity swings; the window, the range and the penalty are varied.</li></ul></div>
<div class="lx-case-part wide"><p class="lx-eyebrow">6 · What came out, and where it holds</p>
<blockquote class="lx-excerpt" data-source="excerpt:ghg"><p>Longer optimization windows and wider adjustment ranges increased the reduction in attributed emissions, most in renewable-rich and diverse grids.</p><p>In grids with diverse generation resources, expanding the adjustment range from ±5% to ±8% can boost carbon reductions from 1.19% to 1.64%.</p><p>In the reported scenarios, reductions in attributed emissions were on the order of one to two percent of regional totals or less.</p><p>Regions with low intensity fluctuation were more sensitive to the cost of regulating load.</p><p>Reductions are computed under average-emission-intensity accounting with perfect foresight; they are not estimates of the consequential (marginal) system response.</p><footer>Approved excerpt of: Li et al. (2025), <a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.crsus.2025.100367">Cell Reports Sustainability</a>.</footer></blockquote>
<p class="lx-hint">Holds when: each hour keeps its average intensity, and the whole window is known in advance. Leaves out: which plants respond.</p></div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<table class="cf-two">
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Factor</th><th scope="col">How it is built</th><th scope="col">The question it answers</th><th scope="col">Moving 10 MWh from 06:00 to 03:00</th></tr></thead>

<tr><th scope="row"><span class="lx-term" data-term="marginal-emission-factor">Marginal</span> (t CO₂ per MWh)</th><td data-l="How it is built">the CO₂ of the plant that serves one more MWh</td><td data-l="The question it answers">What do the plants emit differently if I change my use?</td><td data-l="Moving 10 MWh from 06:00 to 03:00">0.0 t</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p class="lx-hint">Shifting cuts what the plants emit when it moves use away from a dirtier marginal plant, toward spare wind and sun or a cleaner plant. The marginal plant is <a href="08-merit-order.html">lesson 8</a>'s idea.</p>
</div>
<div class="lx-xcard">
<header class="lx-x-head"><h3>Slide the adjustment range</h3></header>
<div class="explainer" data-explainer="ghg">
<ol class="ex-fallback lx-ex-static"><li>Each hour of the grid has an average emission intensity.</li><li>The model moves part of the load from high-intensity hours to low-intensity hours in the same window, within an allowed range, and keeps total use unchanged.</li><li>Attributed emissions fall by the load moved times the intensity gap between those hours.</li><li>Because the range is limited, the reduction is modest; it grows with a wider range and a longer window.</li></ol>
</div>
<p class="lx-hint">A separate example with stylized numbers, from the course author's open explainer: not the study's data or results.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">It counts each hour at its average intensity, so it shows attributed emissions only.</p>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>Marginal emission factors from a model</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- In a dispatch model, an hour's marginal emission factor is the change in total CO₂ when that hour's demand grows by one MWh.
- The toy reads it off each hour's dispatch; a linear program finds it by solving again with one more MWh.
- It holds for a small change only, and it jumps between plants from hour to hour, so real estimates come from dispatch models or from statistics on years of hourly data.
- Putting carbon in the model: caps, prices, frontiers and procurement rules (M6, upcoming in the Modeler tier) takes this further.

:::

```{=html}
<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="cf6-myth">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="lowest-average" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “Moving use into an hour with a lower average CO₂ per MWh always lowers what the plants emit.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. In Prairie Town, moving 10 MWh from 06:00 to 03:00 lowers the average-factor count by 0.3 t, yet the plants emit the same: the combined-cycle plant is on the margin in both hours.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="spare-sun" data-answer="fact">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “Moving use out of a gas hour into an hour when wind or sun is being spilled lowers what the plants emit.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Fact, up to the spilled amount.</p><p>At 14:00 Prairie Town spills 25 MWh of wind and sun, so 10 MWh moved there from 20:00 cut the peaker's CO₂ by 5.5 t; beyond the spill, the next plant serves it.</p></details>
</div>
</div>
<div class="lx-card lx-case-try">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Try it yourself</p>
<p class="lx-hint">Optional, about 30 minutes; needs Python on your computer (<a href="b02-python-data.html">lesson B2</a>).</p>
<ul>
<li>Run <code>examples/strategies.py</code>: it compares a month, a quarter and a year as the window on four synthetic regions. Which kind of grid gains most from a longer window?</li>
<li>Write the synthetic regions with <code>ghg-framework synthetic my_inputs/</code>. Then run <code>ghg-framework run my_inputs/ --region Mixed --limit 0.05</code>, and again with <code>--limit 0.08</code>. Compare <code>reduction_pct</code>.</li>
<li>Then say why neither run can tell you which plant would change its output.</li>
</ul>
<p><a href="https://github.com/Henryutd2021/ghg-load-regulation">ghg-load-regulation</a>: public example repository · MIT licence · synthetic data.</p>
</div>
```
